steps.text: Cook pasta in a large pot of boiling water until al dente. Drain, and rinse in cold water.
In a small bowl, mix together oil, lemon juice, basil, garlic salt, and black pepper.
In a large bowl, combine pasta, tomatoes, green pepper, onion, cucumber, and black olives. Add dressing, and toss to coat. Chill in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Vegetarian Greek Pasta Salad
raw_recipe.description: Penne pasta has great company in this robust salad that is hearty enough to serve as an entree. Tomatoes, cucumbers, green peppers, sweet onion and black olives are tossed with the pasta and an herbed oil and lemon juice dressing.
raw_recipe.name: Vegetarian Greek Pasta Salad

review.reviewBody: I love this recipe...although I've made a few slight changes to it. I use spiral pasta (tri-colored if available) and add 8 oz. feta cheese. It's best to get the block kind of feta and break it up into big chunks b/c when you mix the whole salad, it'll break up the feta. Already crumbled feta breaks down too much. Also, try olive oil instead of veggie oil and 1 tablespoon red wine vinegar instead of lemon juice or half the lemon juice and a little red wine vinegar. I sometimes sprinkle garlic salt instead of regular and a little oregano.

I thought this was a very good salad, with some changes to the dressing. Personally I omitted the olives, not an olive fan. I used rotini pasta (14.5oz box) instead of the penne and used a small Walla Walla onion. The changes I made to the dressing was to add 1/3 cup seasoned rice vinegar, 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, a little over 1/2 tsp salt and 1 tsp crushed garlic, 1 1/2 tsp sweet basil and some generous shakes of parsley. I would highly recommend letting it marinate overnight before eating it to allow the flavors to blend better (I made it last night and it tasted way better this afternoon). I also added a little crumbled goat cheese to my bowl and a few more shakes of rice vinegar after serving myself. Might need to up the vinegar a little more next time. With all those changes it was excellent.

Delicious paired with grilled salmon. I did use a half tablespoon of fresh lemon juice with a half tablespoon of white wine vinegar in the dressing. I also used high quality olive oil. Plus a teaspoon of Italian seasoning. I included an 8 oz. container of crumbled feta as well. I also only used 12 oz. of penne because that is what I had in the pantry. I wondered if the dressing would be enough but it was plenty. I might have made a bit more and increased the veggies if I had used a 16 oz. package of pasta. Delicious!

Great recipe base.I did double all ingredients except the pasta. I used olive oil and kalamata olives in place of vegetable oil and black olives - if using kalamata olives be careful about adding more salt. Kalamat olive are much more salty than black olives. I also added some Greek oregano,red wine vinegar and halved cherry tomatoes.I broiled chicken breasts that had marinated in Greek dressing and sliced them to add to this salad. This salad was great and of course, even better the next day. Thanks Sara!
I’ve made this a million times and love it! Double the dressing and it’s perfect. I add feta too. Yum!

Good...but needed some help. I halved the recipe, but once I tasted it, I decided to add an extra 1/8c olive oil, 1/8c red wine vinegar, fresh ground black pepepr and 4 cloves of crushed garlic. That was the extra kick it needed. It was fantastic with those additions.

A couple notes- The recipe says it serves 8, however if you are cooking for a large gathering with other food items (burgers and the like), it actually serves about 16-20 people. I doubled the recipe for about 30 people, and still had plenty left over. When making the dressing, add the dry ingredients (salt & pepper) directly to the pasta salad. Because they were heavy, they fell to the bottom of the vinaigrette mixture and could not be poured out completely into the pasta. I did what another suggested and used olive oil and red wine vinegar, and also added Feta cheese. I also used fresh basil. Next time I will try scallions instead of sweet onions. Overall, it got good reviews. This recipe is definitely a keeper. Thanks!

I made this recipe on 3 separate occasions. The first time I made this Greek pasta salad, I found myself adding more and more vinegar. Now I add 1/4 cup of vinegar ( I never have lemon on hand and if I do 1 teaspoon is not nearly enough). The Greek pastas I love has that big tangy flavor and that's what I was looking for. Also, I substitute olive oil instead of vegetable oil. Instead of 2 tomatoes, use cherry tomatoes! Go buck on the spices, don't be shy to shower the pasta salad with garlic powder, oregano or dried basil! AND DONT FORGET TO ADD FETA CHEESE!! THIS IS AN ABSOLUTE MUST! Beautiful for any event, whether it be a BBQ or work party.

This recipe was rated a 3/5 because its a good starter recipe, you just need to build on it to suit your personal tastes.

I make this pasta salad every time we have a large party (which is often) or a potluck. It is a welcome change to pasta salad, and it is usually completely gone by the end of the evening. I also use olive oil, fresh minced garlic and dried oregano. Then sprinkle the whole thing with feta cheese. Always a winner!

I made this using WHOLE WHEAT pasta and, um, it was pretty tasteless - DESPITE the fact that I used olive oil instead of veg oil, Kalamata Olives instead of black, and added extra lemon juice. SOOOO, I kept reading the reviews and someone had added Balsamic Vinegar - BINGO!!!! THAT IS THE MISSING INGREDIENT - yummy now with the bite of the vinegar!
I used fresh basil and then I sprinkled feta cheese on it before serving. Also I used some fresh garlic a red pepper. It was FANTASTIC

Mine came out a little onion-y but I just used whatever I had at the house. It might not’ve been the right variety of onion. All in all, I appreciate that this recipe was easy and straightforward. Thanks!
Easy and delicious. I added hard boiled eggs to provide protein and make this dish a summer favorite.
This is terrific! I added some parmesan cheese, but other than that followed the recipe to a T. Definitely will make again.
VERY BLAND as others have said. I added a bunch of feta cheese and Italian dressing. It turned out pretty good after that. If you have a large onion I would suggest only using half.
seems to be missing something just not sure what
Excellent pasta salad! Didn't change a thing except I added a bit more salt once everything was mixed. Didn't add the pepper as I didn't have it in the house.
